title: Brioche Bread and Butter Pudding
subtitle: Enriched brioche in a vanilla custard, baked until just set and golden
excerpt: A richer version of the classic bread and butter pudding, using buttered brioche slices in a vanilla-cream custard and baked until the custard just sets and the tops of the bread turn golden.
sourceNotes: A richer variant of the Mrs Beeton classic, using buttery brioche in place of white bread. The brioche absorbs the custard more lightly than white bread and puffs during baking, giving a noticeably more custardy result. The technique is otherwise unchanged.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate before baking. Add 5 minutes to the baking time if going in from cold.

content.text: Brioche bread and butter pudding is the classic white-bread version made with buttered brioche slices instead. The enriched dough absorbs custard differently, giving a lighter result with a golden, slightly crisp top. Rest it for 20 minutes before baking to let the bread soak through.

items.prepNote: softened, for spreading, plus extra for the dish

content.text: Preheat the oven to 160°C fan. Butter a 1.5-litre baking dish generously. Butter the brioche slices on one side. Arrange them in the dish, overlapping slightly, buttered side up. The slices should fill the dish but not be packed in too tightly, you need the custard to flow between them.

Whisk the cream, milk, whole eggs, extra yolks, sugar, and vanilla together in a large jug until combined and the sugar has dissolved. Pour the custard slowly over the brioche, letting it flow between the slices. Press the brioche down gently with the back of a spoon so each slice is saturated. Leave to soak for 20 minutes before baking.

Bake at 160°C fan for 40 to 45 minutes. The custard should be just set, it will have a faint wobble in the very centre when you nudge the dish, and the exposed tops of the brioche should be deep golden. Remove from the oven. If using the marmalade glaze, brush it over the top immediately and allow it to set for a few minutes. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm from the dish.

items.symptom: The custard has not set after 45 minutes
items.cause: The oven temperature is running low, or the dish was very cold when it went in.
items.fix: Return to the oven for a further 5 to 10 minutes. The custard sets as it cools slightly too, so a faint wobble in the centre is correct, it should not be entirely liquid.

items.symptom: The bread is floating out of the custard
items.cause: The brioche was not pressed down firmly during the soaking rest.
items.fix: Press the slices down firmly before baking, weighting them with a plate if needed during the 20-minute rest.

items.symptom: The top is browning too fast before the custard has set
items.cause: Oven is running hot, or the dish is close to the top element.
items.fix: Tent loosely with foil and continue baking until the custard sets.

content.text: Best eaten on the day of baking, served warm from the oven. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1 day, covered. Reheat individual portions in the oven at 160°C for 10 minutes, or in a microwave until just hot through, the texture will be softer when reheated.
